correctness.rationale: Both norms attain extrema at sign vertices because the polynomial is square-free. For each sign pair, symmetry eliminates cross edges and reduces the bilinear evaluation to the difference of two internal-block quadratic values. A block of size <=2 can negate its internal value, proving the optimal factor 1 for n<=5. The only new six-dimensional 3+3 cut has three sign-flip averages equal to minus one-third of its all-ones quadratic value on each triple, giving two estimates that imply factor 3/2. Opposite-signed triangle blocks give exact norms 8 and 12. Exact rational coefficient identities for all 5456 sign pairs n=2..6 were independently checked from packaged CHECK.py. The theorem asserts no exact higher-dimensional value.

value.rationale: This exact natural restricted polynomial/multilinear norm comparison identifies the minimal dimension where decoupling changes the sharp constant and computes the full 50-percent jump. It exposes a previously unresolved-looking discrete geometry not captured by unrestricted polarization or SDP bounds. The explicit two-triangle extremizer and universal short proof make the dimension threshold reusable in finite Boolean quadratic optimization; this is more than a coefficient normalization or isolated numerical experiment.
